category_title: Struggling readers supported by literal comprehension scaffolding
minimal_context: The student and teacher are discussing a self-selected book about a pancake eating contest during a one-on-one reading conference.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's discuss your book. What happened during the pancake eating contest?

STUDENT: He wanted to eat the most pancakes.

TUTOR: What did he do with the juice?

STUDENT: He didn’t know that they could drink a lot of juice, more than him.

TUTOR: How would you describe the way the character acted when he did that?

STUDENT: They were silly.

options.A: Ask follow-up questions of the student during one-to-one reading conferences about the self-selected book.
options.B: Provide a ticket for each behavioral expectation met during the conference, exchangeable for a small reward.
options.C: Provide access to socially appropriate sensory stimulation during the reading conference, such as a stress-relief ball.
options.D: Use a digital note-taking app to take notes, organize reading responses, and archive past book discussions.
